Rules / Correctness

SK2173 is not { } is a null check written backwards

A not { } pattern with no type, no positional clause, no subpatterns and no designation matches exactly the null values, so it is null spelled in a way that reads as its opposite.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

{ } matches every non-null value, so not { } matches every null one. The word on the page is not, the reader takes it as "has something", and the pattern means "has nothing". x is null says it in four characters with no inversion to hold in your head. ⚠ `{ }` matches a boxed struct and a non-null `Nullable<T>` as well as a reference, and the rewrite keeps all of that — is null on a T? is !HasValue, which is exactly what is not { } was already testing.

Example

Instead of:

if (result is not { }) { return Failure(); }

Write:

if (result is null) { return Failure(); }

When it does not fire

⚠ The one shape that would break the rewrite cannot be written, and the compiler is what guarantees it: int value in value is not { } is CS8518, "an expression of type 'int' can never match the provided pattern", and so is a T constrained to struct. There is therefore no compiling program in which is not { } stands on something is null would reject, and the rule needs no semantic model to know it — measured on a probe, not reasoned from the specification. An unconstrained T accepts both spellings and is reported. ⚠ The pattern must be empty in all four ways. not { Length: 0 } has a subpattern, not string { } has a type, not (1, 2) is positional and not { } x binds a designation; none of them is a null check and none is reported. The registration is on the not pattern itself, so the rule reaches a case not { }: label, a switch arm and a nested subpattern as well as a bare is, and a parenthesised not ({ }) is declined because the parentheses are a choice about grouping that the fix would have to unpick. ⚠ A comment or a preprocessor directive inside the pattern's span withdraws the finding rather than the fix, so that no positive fixture can produce a report the fix cannot serve; the fix replaces the whole not { } span with null, and a fix that silently deleted a comment out of that span would be a fix nobody can review. Generated code is excluded.
